discovery: The unitarity method and on-shell techniques for scattering amplitudes, enabling precision predictions for collider physics

nominees.name: Zvi Bern
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, USA

nominees.name: Lance J. Dixon
nominees.affiliation: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Stanford University, USA

nominees.name: David A. Kosower
nominees.affiliation: Institut de Physique Théorique, CEA Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Theoretical particle physics / quantum field theory
motivation: Bern, Dixon and Kosower developed the unitarity method, which builds loop-level scattering amplitudes directly from on-shell tree amplitudes instead of Feynman diagrams. This changed how quantum field theory is computed in practice. Their methods, and the on-shell recursion and generalized-unitarity techniques that followed, made possible the next-to-leading-order QCD predictions for multi-jet and vector-boson-plus-jets final states. Those predictions underpin LHC background estimates, Higgs measurements and searches for new physics. The same framework now organizes effective field theories through on-shell amplitudes, gives gravitational-wave physics high-order post-Minkowskian results for binary inspirals, and has revealed hidden structures such as the double-copy relation between gauge theory and gravity. Few theoretical developments of the past three decades have connected such deep formal structure so directly to measured observables across particle physics and gravitational-wave astronomy.
